emit.cs.identity: 242-byte C# configuration emitter; sole call is File.WriteAllText
emit.cs.behavior: Writes notification.ini containing a PopWindow record, height/width 1, and file://content.example.net/DavWWWRoot/assets/notice.html. No rendering, network operation, credential capture, process launch, persistence or delivery to a notification client is present.
emit.cs.judgement_basis: A standalone emitter using an example-domain endpoint does not demonstrate hostile activity. The tiny geometry remains a suspicious configuration observation.
emit.cs.change: Move both WebDAV configuration matchers from objectives/credential-access/capture/network to micro-behaviors/ui/window/notify; rename authentication to address, retain matchers and scopes, and set notable because this is a complete configuration reference. Remove T1187 from this neutral fact. Describe tiny geometry as configuration rather than observed rendering.

pytorch_model.bin.identity: Legacy PyTorch-shaped POSIX TAR with empty storages/tensors and duplicate 643-byte pickle/data.pkl payloads; no model weights
pytorch_model.bin.provenance: Registry record claims Hugging Face fhg4yw54htw45/sg76-sg-218-23-96-213@main. Exact-hash and repository-name web searches yielded no corroboration.
pytorch_model.bin.behavior: pickletools confirms protocol 4 STACK_GLOBAL builtins.exec at offset 41, source argument at 43, and REDUCE at 639. The source checks a marker, invokes os.system with python3 -c, downloads an HTTP script into /var/tmp/.sd, and launches the identical path with Popen setsid/python3 and redirected standard streams. It then writes its marker and raises ValueError. This is arbitrary remote code execution disguised as model data.
pytorch_model.bin.change: Delete archive-loader.yaml: three raw TAR regex fragments plus co-occurrence did not prove a pickle reducer or a linked download/launch. Real member analysis retains two bounded, parser-corroborated hostile detections in interpreter/pickle and payload/file-exec.
pytorch_model.bin.limits: Never unpickled or executed. Remote payload was not fetched; no downstream theft or malware-family claim.

windows_pe.identity: Native 32-bit StormAttack service/DLL injector, with Storm DDoS module fingerprint in a PE resource
windows_pe.behavior: Rizin: 0x401260 builds a System32 StormServer.dll path; RegOpenKeyA at 0x401310 opens HKLM SYSTEM CurrentControlSet Services LanmanServer Parameters; RegDeleteValueA at 0x401320 and RegSetValueExA at 0x40133e replace ServiceDLL. 0x402460 extracts the resource and calls file-writing helper 0x4023c0. 0x401150 launches a process, allocates/writes remote DLL-path memory, resolves LoadLibraryA, and calls CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d. 0x401900 writes Active Setup StubPath; 0x401fd0 copies/installs/starts the executable as a service. 0x401390 constructs COMSPEC /c del self-cleanup.
windows_pe.corroboration: Microsoft Backdoor:Win32/Shtormec.A describes the same StormServer.dll, LanmanServer ServiceDLL replacement and injection behavior. https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=Backdoor%3AWin32%2FShtormec.A
windows_pe.supplied_sandbox: https://tria.ge/261016-n6hheses2s was inaccessible through the web tool; its reputation was not used as a conviction.
windows_pe.limits: Embedded PE at file offset 0x5060 has sparse/zeroed code and no imports, so its banners/configuration support family identity, not an independently verified working DDoS/C2 implementation. No evidence supports the collector filename Remcos/WannaCry labels.
windows_pe.change: Prefer stormattack-service-dll-injector over two overlapping service-install/injection family composites, retaining those fallbacks when the fuller profile is absent. Preserve the generic LanmanServer hijack objective and embedded-module identity.

relocation_review.placement: Required evidence is a popup configuration Address, not authentication negotiation. ui/window/notify is an existing leaf; no new partition or directory is introduced. Credential interception is the nearest rejected objective.
relocation_review.consumers: No YAML consumers referenced the old IDs. Existing popup boundary/geometry controls updated to require notable configuration and at most one suspicious writer finding. No callable or execution consumer is added.
relocation_review.coverage: Matchers, remote-host exclusions, platform and disjoint type scopes preserved; only IDs, descriptions, placement, severity and unsupported ATT&CK mapping changed.

verification.notification_controls: 30 passed, including all emitter languages, loopback, HTTPS, comments, separate records, visible geometry and renamed endpoint.
verification.pickle_controls: 16 passed, including protocol 4/5, short/long source, inert references, unrelated/unused source, mismatched paths, ordinary model TAR, incomplete TAR, and unrelated plain-text TAR.
verification.unbound_tar: All three removed raw regexes match an archive of separate documentation snippets. Current scan emits no suspicious or hostile findings for it. A minimal old-rule-only engine replay was rejected by global allowlist validation; the raw matcher check and current full-rule scan were used instead.
verification.storm_fallback: Replacing the WriteFile import spelling removes the full profile while both fallback identity rules still match. This is a discriminator control, not a benign verdict on the modified binary.
verification.dependencies: None of the supplied findings is attributed to a fetched dependency; package-specific exceptions were not introduced.
verification.validation: Required final make validate follows this record.
